verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.69
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 6.69

verses.pali: 7. Devatāvagga
verses.english: 7. A God

verses.pali: Devatāsutta
verses.english: A God

verses.pali: Atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho sā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: “Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

verses.pali: Katame cha?
verses.english: What six?

verses.pali: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā—
verses.english: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

verses.pali: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
verses.english: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.”

verses.pali: Idamavoca sā devatā.
verses.english: That’s what that deity said,

verses.pali: Samanuñño satthā ahosi.
verses.english: and the teacher approved.

verses.pali: Atha kho sā devatā “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.
verses.english: Then that deity, knowing that the teacher approved, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, bhikkhave, sā devatā maṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: “Tonight, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, came to me, bowed, stood to one side, and said to me:

verses.pali: ‘chayime, bhante, dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: ‘Sir, these six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.

verses.pali: Katame cha?
verses.english: What six?

verses.pali: Satthugāravatā, dhammagāravatā, saṅghagāravatā, sikkhāgāravatā, sovacassatā, kalyāṇamittatā—
verses.english: Respect for the Teacher, for the teaching, for the Saṅgha, for the training; being easy to admonish, and good friendship.

verses.pali: ime kho, bhante, cha dhammā bhikkhuno aparihānāya saṁvattantī’ti.
verses.english: These six things don’t lead to the decline of a mendicant.’

verses.pali: Idamavoca, bhikkhave, sā devatā.
verses.english: That is what that deity said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
verses.english: Then he bowed and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right side, before vanishing right there.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi.
verses.english: “Sir, this is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.

verses.pali: Idha, bhante, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher and praises such respect.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
verses.english: And they encourage other mendicants who lack such respect to respect the Teacher.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
verses.english: And they praise other mendicants who respect the Teacher at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

verses.pali: Attanā ca dhammagāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the teaching …

verses.pali: saṅghagāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the Saṅgha …

verses.pali: sikkhāgāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the training …

verses.pali: suvaco hoti …
verses.english: They are personally easy to admonish …

verses.pali: kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇamittatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
verses.english: They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
verses.english: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
verses.english: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

verses.pali: Imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta.
verses.english: “Good, good, Sāriputta!

verses.pali: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, sāriputta, imassa mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi.
verses.english: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.

verses.pali: Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu attanā ca satthugāravo hoti satthugāravatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant personally respects the Teacher …

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū na satthugāravā te ca satthugāravatāya samādapeti.
Ye caññe bhikkhū satthugāravā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Attanā ca dhammagāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the teaching …

verses.pali: saṅghagāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the Saṅgha …

verses.pali: sikkhāgāravo hoti …
verses.english: They personally respect the training …

verses.pali: suvaco hoti …
verses.english: They are personally easy to admonish …

verses.pali: kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇamittatāya ca vaṇṇavādī.
verses.english: They personally have good friends, and praise such friendship.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū na kalyāṇamittā te ca kalyāṇamittatāya samādapeti.
verses.english: And they encourage other mendicants who lack good friends to develop good friendship.

verses.pali: Ye caññe bhikkhū kalyāṇamittā tesañca vaṇṇaṁ bhaṇati bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
verses.english: And they praise other mendicants who have good friends at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

verses.pali: Imassa kho, sāriputta, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti.
verses.english: This is how to understand the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.”

verses.pali: Pañcamaṁ.
